scenes.text: Your shadow is not attached to you. It is just light failing to reach the ground where you stand.
scenes.art_prompt: a long shadow of a person stretching across sunlit pavement, crisp

scenes.text: Suppose light took a full second to cross a room. Your shadow would move a second behind you.
scenes.art_prompt: a person walking while their shadow trails behind at an impossible delay, surreal

scenes.text: Reach for a cup and the shadow reaches after. Turn off a lamp and the darkness arrives late.
scenes.art_prompt: a hand reaching for a cup with its shadow arriving late, physics illustration

scenes.text: At the real speed of light, that delay is about a billionth of a second. You would never see it.
scenes.art_prompt: a clock face and a beam of light racing across a room, clean diagram

scenes.text: The world looks instant only because light is fast. Slow it down and every glance becomes a replay.
scenes.art_prompt: a person and their shadow in a sunlit room, quietly resolved

scenes.text: Follow What If Physics for the next question.
scenes.art_prompt: a bright empty street with long afternoon shadows, final wide shot
